title: Is more occupancy always better?
summary: What occupancy buys and when trading it away pays off.

choices.text: Occupancy hides latency: with more warps resident, the SM has more warps ready to issue while others wait on memory.
A kernel at 100% occupancy is necessarily faster than the same kernel at 50%.
A kernel that keeps several independent loads in flight per thread can reach full bandwidth at low occupancy.
Forcing fewer registers per thread to raise occupancy never hurts, because the compiler always finds a way to fit.
Fast matmul kernels often run at low occupancy on purpose: large per-thread tiles in registers raise data reuse.
